name: reladraw
category: A4. Vector, typography, diagrams and stills
role: Text diagram language with author-placed, relative layout; SVG out
notes: 2026-11-27: Lead said 0.32.0; npm showed 0.32.1 (Apache-2.0). Lead's `pnpm add -g` replaced by a local pnpm add in the example.
2026-11-27: Triage: assess. The README warns the syntax changes frequently, so pin the version.
2026-11-27: Gap/units: `gap: N` is scaled (gap: 40 drew about 480 px), so tune against the rendered size.
2026-11-27: Toolkit guide skills/reladraw/SKILL.md written from reladraw-stable-layout evidence (0.32.1, macOS arm64); other syntax untested.

evidence.result: v1 (3 nodes, 2 arrows, viewBox 0 0 436 127) and v2 (4 nodes, 3 arrows, viewBox 0 0 453 246) rendered; Source, Layout and SVG box paths identical in both; repeat render byte-identical; check printed no warnings; 900 px raster showed no overlap.
evidence.scope: Adding one node to a three-node chain leaves existing nodes' coordinates unchanged, reladraw 0.32.1, macOS arm64. Not other syntax, larger graphs, label-driven resizing or cross-version output.

summary: A text language where the author says where each node goes (right of, below, gap) and reladraw draws exactly that to SVG with a local CLI (render, check, format, serve). No auto-layout, so a diagram edit does not move unrelated nodes. Pin the version: syntax still changes between releases.
use_when: Over D2 or Graphviz when nodes must keep their positions between diagram versions
Diagram-build animation where each version of the source is a keyframe
avoid_when: Use D2 or Graphviz when automatic layout of many nodes and edges is wanted
Use Mermaid CLI for diagrams embedded in Markdown

assessment.rationale: Apache-2.0, zero runtime dependencies, local CLI renders SVG headlessly. Adds author-controlled placement that D2, Graphviz and Mermaid lack. Young (repo from 2026-09) and syntax unstable, so keep as a candidate.
